question: On 5 December 2003, Italy’s Ministry of Environment and Energy Security launched a strategic environmental assessment (SEA) procedure for the Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC)1. Italy sent the PNIEC2 to the Commission on 3 July 2024, but has not yet informed the public of the results of the strategic environmental assessment3.

Furthermore, the preliminary environmental report on which the Ministry consulted the public did not make any reference to a nuclear programme, other than a mention of research in that field4. However, the PNIEC sent to the Commission assumes the establishment of nuclear capacity from 20355, reaching a capacity of 8 GW by 20506, despite the fact that the public was not consulted on this scenario.
In view of the above: 1.

Has Italy complied with the obligations under recital 18 of Directive 2001/42/EC7 in terms of informing the public and making available the data relating to the PNIEC, including the results of the consultation?

Given that the preliminary plan did not anticipate the establishment of nuclear capacity, has Italy complied with the requirement to give the public effective opportunities to participate in the preparation of the draft plan, in accordance with Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2018/19998 and Article 6 of Directive 2001/42/EC9?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.1.2025) 1. On 3 July 2024, Italy notified the Commission as ‘final’ its updated National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP)1, based on Article 14(2) of the Governance Regulation2. The accompanying letter explains that the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is still ongoing. 2.

Article 10 of the Governance Regulation states that in so far as the SEA Directive3 is applicable, consultations undertaken on the draft NECP in accordance with that Directive shall be deemed to satisfy the obligations to consult the public under the Regulation.

According to Article 6(2) of the SEA Directive, the public shall be given an early and effective opportunity to express their opinion on the draft plans and the accompanying environmental reports before the adoption of the plans.

The Commission’s recommendations4 on the Italian draft NECP reflect the crucial importance of a wide regional consultation and an early and inclusive consultation on the plan, including effective public participation with sufficient information and time5.

The Commission, in its ongoing assessment of the updated NECPs, will assess whether Italy has taken due account of the Commission’s recommendations in drafting the final updated NECP. In any event, Member States are primarily responsible for the correct implementation of EU law.
In accordance with the principle of effective judicial protection, it is for the national judge to ensure the compatibility of national measures with EU law.

3 Directive 2001/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 June 2001 on the assessment of the effects of certain plans and programmes on the environment, (OJ L 197, 21.7.2001, p. 30). 4 Recommendations issued pursuant to Article 34 of the Governance Regulation, https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/af5bd599-e8b5-49fd-a498dc00d6b81a0f_en?filename=Recommendation_draft_updated_NECP_Italy_2023.
